主要内容: Babson College's M&A survey indicates middle-market M&A activity remained stable in 2013, with strong deal volume but slower small business growth. The services sector led with increased activity in e-commerce, health, and aerospace. Small business M&A grew more slowly, with EBITDA valuations rising 0.5 times over 2012 but no expected increase this year. Private equity buyers may rise due to improved debt availability. Strategic buyers seek more due diligence expertise. Sellers must prepare quickly to close deals within six months. Legal and deal expertise are critical for success. Financing for buyers is growing, with terms becoming more acceptable for both lenders and borrowers. Yields on mezzanine debt dropped to 12-14% from historical averages of 15-20%, and financing costs declined as the volume of financial buyer deals increased. SBA loans rebounded strongly, particularly from community banks, supporting small business deal growth. The percentage of equity required by qualified buyers of small businesses rose from 20% to 25%.
